issues.description: Constructor parameter order for class ExcellenceLand is inconsistent between the problem specification and the solution. The UML and task text in the problem statement define the attributes (in this order): excellencyLevel (double), excellentEnough (boolean), and the rides association (List<Ride>) and require a public constructor that takes the attributes in the same order. The solution declares the constructor as: public ExcellenceLand(List<Ride> rides, boolean excellentEnough, double excellencyLevel) — i.e. parameters are ordered (List<Ride>, boolean, double). This mismatch will cause automated checks that validate constructor parameter order to fail and will confuse students implementing the constructor according to the UML/task description.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the ExcellenceLand constructor parameter order to match the UML/task order: (double excellencyLevel, boolean excellentEnough, List<Ride> rides). Example: public ExcellenceLand(double excellencyLevel, boolean excellentEnough, List<Ride> rides) { this.excellencyLevel = excellencyLevel; this.excellentEnough = excellentEnough; this.rides = rides; } Ensure the parameter order in the constructor signature and assignment matches the problem statement so automated tests and students' expectations align.
